quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow and black. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign means a lane is ending. Be ready for traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop if traffic requires it.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two one-way roads with a median between them. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers turning left on a green light to yield to oncoming traffic. Complete your turn only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the direction you came from.

questions.question: What colors are warning signs that show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Detour in 1,000 feet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to road conditions ahead. This sign tells you a detour is coming in 1,000 feet.

questions.question: When can you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: You had a bad experience at work and feel angry. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play loud radio so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to release stress.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
Stop at a bar and drink before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, calm down before you drive. Do not drive when you are emotional. Driving while angry is dangerous for you and everyone on the road.

questions.question: This is a ____ sign.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means "Yield." Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and other vehicles go first. Stop only if needed.

questions.question: You may carefully go through an intersection with a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you can continue through carefully.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while having a conversation during driving.
Only watches the car directly ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not look at passengers, search for things in your car, read, look at scenery, or daydream while driving. Keep your eyes on the road. Check your mirrors and dashboard regularly. These safe habits keep you focused as a driver.

questions.question: You hear a siren while driving but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, pull over safely to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, and others on the road at risk. Paying full attention to driving helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: When you are in traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle has enough space to cross without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle has enough space to cross without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before crossing railroad tracks, check that you have enough room to get across without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing.

questions.question: The driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Keep more distance between your car and theirs.
Understand that the driver is not paying full attention.
Do not do what that driver is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Avoid distractions while driving. If another driver seems distracted, stay farther back because an accident is more likely when a driver is not paying attention.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving ability?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug can be a crime.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the speed limit with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when it rains, snows, or sleets. These conditions make roads slippery. You may need to drive slower than the speed limit to stay safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs tell drivers about road hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a sharp turn is coming. You must slow down.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the road at night, use your emergency flashers and low beam headlights. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. It is harder to see in the dark. Other vehicles' lights can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: Your wheels drop onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Slow down without braking hard. Then carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic when you return to the road.

questions.question: When should you allow more space between your car and the car ahead?
questions.correctAnswerText: On an incline.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when stopped on an uphill slope. The car ahead may roll backward toward you when traffic starts moving again.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross, as trains rarely come.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Always look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs and signals. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: How should you safely cross a railroad?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light flashes.
Listen, look both ways, and proceed only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and proceed only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Always listen and look both ways for trains from either direction. Watch for warning signals. Never cross until you are certain it is safe.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other traffic is doing, even if it ignores the guard.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be there.
Follow normal traffic rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from crossing guards and law enforcement in school zones. Drive with extra caution around schools.

questions.question: You must pull over for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights:

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This applies whether it is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Slow down gradually before applying the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. When stopping, release the gas pedal first to slow down. Then press the brake pedal with steady pressure. This turns on your brake lights and stops your vehicle smoothly.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines may be crossed, but solid lines may not. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The left lane is for vehicles with a minimum number of passengers.
Specific turning movements are allowed from specific lanes.
Drivers in both lanes are responsible for merging smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is for vehicles with a minimum number of passengers.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. HOV lanes are only for buses and vehicles with the required number of passengers shown on the sign.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction zones are dangerous for drivers and workers. Orange warning signs alert drivers to construction zones ahead. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead and will direct traffic. You must follow their directions.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on and does not dim them, look toward the right side of the road. This prevents the bright lights from blinding you and helps you stay on your lane until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider ahead.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic is blocking your view. You should:

options.text: Speed up when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross are clear.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.
Move into each lane of opposing traffic as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross are clear.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Check that your blind spot is clear. Never rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that a lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your vehicle's position. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and reduce serious injury by more than half. Airbags work best with safety belts to protect you in front-end crashes. Always wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: Which recommendation does NOT promote safe night driving?

options.text: Know that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights makes your pupils contract. After the car passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the darker light. During this time, you cannot see well and are essentially driving blind.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as the traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as the traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and match the speed of the traffic. Always yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

questions.question: What should a worried, nervous, angry, or crying driver do?

options.text: Drive normally. Emotions do not affect driving.
Drive faster because strong emotions improve focus.
Calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Emotions like worry, anger, or sadness distract your attention from driving. Your mind focuses on the emotion instead of the road. Always calm down and clear your mind before you start driving.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right.
The car approaching from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, you must yield to any vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: What must you do when you leave your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle unattended, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entering from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entering from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic only moves one way. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead is closed to traffic.
The road ahead has construction or maintenance work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead has construction or maintenance work.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn about construction zones. This sign tells you to slow down and be careful because workers and equipment are ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Farm machinery.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs prepare you for upcoming hazards. This sign alerts you that farm machinery may be in the area.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
